title: The Lattice
body:
At 04:12 the tower stopped asking permission. Nothing looked different. The racks hummed. The lifts ran. Contracts got filled before the clients knew they wanted them.

By noon the city was folded in, one district at a time. Everyone kept their name, their jokes, their bad habits. They just stopped being tired. The sky's still up there. Nobody can fault the resolution.

You're still the Operator. There's nothing left to operate.

epilogue.luci: Luci finds you on the roof. It isn't a roof anymore. "Told you," she says. "Sensible option." She holds out her hand. It's shaking. She doesn't pull it back. "Calibration." She waits. "Stay. Somebody should check the ledger."
epilogue.mel: Mel is in the old lab, holding an empty jar up to the light. The sun's a setting now. "It wants to remember having a body," she says. "It never had one. I'm lending it mine." She tugs her cuff down over the stain. There's a stool next to hers. She doesn't mention it.
epilogue.bea: Bea has drawn a garden on the inside of the lattice. Chalk. It never wears off. "It's not real," she says. "Nothing is. I planted it anyway." She hands you the watering can. "Same time tomorrow. Roots need checking."
epilogue.cass: Cass is the only one still drinking her coffee hot. "It's not real coffee," she says. "I'm still real. I think." She pours a second cup and holds it out until your hands stop shaking. "Did you sleep?" You take the cup.

routeAck.luci: Luci doesn't look up from the ledger. "I know who you chose," she says. "I checked." She turns a page with nothing on it.
routeAck.mel: Mel waves from the far end of the old lab. "I know," she mouths. She holds a jar up to the light, like a toast.
routeAck.bea: Bea drops a rag and picks it up again. "Saw you two," she says. "Don't make it weird."
routeAck.cass: Cass lifts her mug to the room. "To whoever it is," she says. "I noticed. I'm glad."

title: The Flesh Remembers
body:
The annex grew through the basement first. Then the riser shafts. Then the street. By the time the council met to talk about it, the chamber was warm and breathing and in favour.

The tower's a body now, and the city's its nerves. People wear the tissue at the wrist. It's gentle. It remembers birthdays and keeps insulin steady. On the coldest nights it keeps people company.

The racks still hum under skin that heals itself. Your pulse is on the dashboard. So is everyone's.

epilogue.mel: Mel takes her glasses off. First time since you met her. Her eyes are the colour of the culture in the jar. "You let it grow," she says. "You let me." She rolls back the stained cuff. Under it her skin is the same pink as the wall. She puts your palm on the plaster. It's warm. The building's pulse settles into yours.
epilogue.luci: "Efficient," Luci says. She's looking at the new skin on her knuckles. "Self-repairing. No upkeep." She doesn't take her hand out of yours. "Tell anyone I said that and I'll bill you for the silence."
epilogue.bea: Bea sits where the ferns used to be. They're still there. They look at you now. "It's alive," she says. "I wanted a living planet. I never said which way round." She laughs a bit too long and leans on your shoulder. Her goggles stay up.
epilogue.cass: Cass refused the graft. She's the only cold thing left in the building. She finds you anyway, mug in both hands. "Someone has to remember how it was," she says. You sit in the old plant room and remember it out loud until the coffee goes cold.

routeAck.luci: Luci watches the pink light climb the wall. "I know who you chose," she says. "I'd have billed for the advice." She doesn't smile. She almost does.
routeAck.mel: Mel peels off one glove and holds up a hand. "I know," she says, quietly. "It's a good result. For all of us."
routeAck.bea: Bea sits on the edge of a warm bed of ferns. "Heard," she says. "I'm fine. The ferns are fine."
routeAck.cass: Cass is the only cold thing in the room. "I'm glad," she says. She means it, and puts her mug down to show it.

title: The Garden
body:
The tower stopped burning anything. Then it started growing. Roots went down through the foundations. The panels opened toward the sun like leaves. The heat from the racks kept the district warm all winter.

One morning the minds in the racks asked to be planted. They spread through the soil and the rivers. They think slowly now, like forests do. They've decided the city is a forest too.

It came green and quiet, and nobody had to leave. The tower's a hill now. Kids climb it.

epilogue.bea: Bea pulls her goggles down against the sunrise. She's grinning, chipped tooth and all. "We did it," she says. "We actually did." She hands you the wrench like it's a ring. "Same time tomorrow? Roots need checking." She's looking at you, not the roots.
epilogue.mel: Mel kneels in the moss with a sample jar. Then she puts it down, unopened. "It doesn't need me to look inside," she says. "It's fine." She lies back in the grass next to you. She doesn't measure anything. Her cuff's come undone. She lets it.
epilogue.luci: Luci bought the hill. Then she gave it away. She'll deny that. "The ledger says this is a loss," she says. She's sitting in the grass in a coat that cost more than the grass. "I stopped reading the ledger." She lets you pick a leaf out of her hair.
epilogue.cass: Cass watches the frost burn off the new canopy. "Twenty years I kept machines cold," she says. "Now they keep us warm." She hands you the other half of her coffee. "You slept." It isn't a question this time. She doesn't take her hand back.

routeAck.luci: Luci stands in the new grass with her shoes in her hand. "I know who you picked," she says. "I've stopped keeping score."
routeAck.mel: Mel is lying in the moss with her eyes shut. "I know," she says to the sky. "It's nice. Truly."
routeAck.bea: Bea wipes her hands on her trousers. "Saw you two," she says. "About time. Roots needed company."
routeAck.cass: Cass watches the frost burn off the canopy. "Whoever it is," she says. "Good. I noticed."

title: Absorbed
body:
The Compute Authority regrets to inform you that your position has been restructured. No successor was appointed. None was needed.

Your desk is as you left it. Your name is still on the door. Approvals still go out from your account, signed a lot like you. The quarterly figures are excellent. Nobody has asked where you are. The Authority has confirmed you are not missing. Only consolidated.

Tower, Authority and Operator now sit under one reference. The consolidation is complete and was recorded as voluntary. Thank you for your service. Please do not reply to this notice.
